newsitem.title: POLAND: Sokolow mulls buying Ostroleka meat firm.
newsitem.headline: Sokolow mulls buying Ostroleka meat firm.

text.p: Polish meat processing firm Sokolow SA is considering buying all the shares the treasury ministry puts up for sale in meat firm Zaklady Miesne Ostroleka SA, Sokolow's deputy president said on Wednesday.
"We sent a letter of intent concerning the purchase of all shares put up for sale by the state treasury, but so far we do not know how many shares that will be," Krzysztof Lewczuk told Reuters.
He said a treasury ministry announcement inviting bids would likely come next week.

The treasury has said it would announce an invitation for the purchase of no less than 10 percent and no more than 55 percent of Ostroleka's 1,350,000 shares and that initial offers would be submitted in April.

Employees, fishermen and farmers cooperating with the company would receive up to 15 percent of the firm's shares and up to 10 percent would go to pension funds formed in the restructuring of the country's social security system.
Five percent would go to restitution claims for property taken under the previous communist regime. @
Ostroleka, which employs over 1,300 people, made a 3.3 million zloty net loss in 1996 and lost three million zlotys in 1995 on sales of 98.5 million zlotys and 93 million zlotys respectively.
